title: Sam Altman says he's not worried about OpenAI's IPO plan
excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the ChatGPT maker will eventually go public and AI investors are "pretty bullish."
content_html:
By Brent D. Griffiths

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-16T22:06:52.187Z

Sam Altman shrugged off the idea that OpenAI could become the Lyft to Anthropic's Uber.

"That is not a worry," Altman said on Monday during a live interview at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World event.

Altman's response to the question about OpenAI's chief rival generated audible laughter in the room. In 2019, Lyft went public before Uber, and its shares outperformed its ride-share rival's on their respective first days of trading. But Uber got the last laugh and today is worth roughly 22 times Lyft by market cap.

Altman said that the narrative about investor demand is different than what he's seeing. He said that "there is a lot of skepticism from journalists" but that investors remain "pretty bullish."

"I get that you have to write something every day, and there's got to be all this, you know, this fight and that one, and this winner, and this loser, and what's happening here and there — but the macro trend and the value being created, I'm not at all worried about there not being a huge amount," he said.

The OpenAI chief reiterated his view that the ChatGPT maker will eventually go public. Anthropic publicly released its S-1 on October 26 and is expected to debut on Nasdaq later this week.

That doesn't mean that being a public company will be easy, Altman said.

"I think there are real downsides to being public," he said. "And it's a very volatile time in our industry with high-stakes, consequential decisions to make around safety and how society is going to interact with this technology. And there are doubtless things that are easier as a private company."

Altman said it's "directionally a good thing" that more investors want exposure to the AI boom. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar recently said that bringing the company public is in line with OpenAI's mission to bring super intelligence to everyone.

Friar also said that OpenAI is still targeting a 2027 IPO and that the tech backlash that helped power the blue tsunami in the midterms hasn't "dramatically changed" the company's thinking.

"Look, we are paid as operators to manage scenarios," Friar told CNBC earlier this month. "I don't think there was something that dramatically changed for us."
